# 1. Application Description

## 1.1 Purpose and Users

The Agentic Service Operations Intelligence Platform answers operational questions about a field-service business in plain English: quality incidents, service-level performance, customer sentiment, and expected work volume. It returns a verified answer without the user writing a query or waiting for an analyst.

The platform runs on a fully synthetic dataset of about 20,000 service requests, from September 2023 through August 2026, that models a field-service dispatch operation.

The platform has two audiences:

- Business users. Operations leaders who ask questions and act on the answers (Section 3).
- Operators. Whoever runs, maintains, and recovers the system (Sections 2 and 4 through 7).

## 1.2 What the Platform Answers

Each question goes to one of three specialist capabilities.

| **Capability**     | **Answers**                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Does not answer**                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Quality reporting  | Incident counts and rate; SLA compliance; first-time fix rate; drivers of repeat visits. Broken down by account, region, service type, technician, incident type, or severity; filtered to one region, account, or technician. | Metrics outside these definitions; areas other than the four regions (Northeast, Southeast, Central, West), such as states or cities. |
| Customer sentiment | Counts and shares of positive, neutral, negative, and mixed feedback; comments flagged for human review; significant change in the negative share over months or quarters; up to three example comments. One region or all.    | Sentiment by account, technician, or service type; themes or causes behind sentiment.                                                 |
| Volume forecasting | Weekly request volume up to 26 weeks ahead, in total or by service type, with an 80% range and measured historical error.                                                                                                      | Past periods; forecasts of SLA performance, incidents, or sentiment; forecasts by region, account, or technician.                     |

Forecast coverage is deliberately limited. A forecast is shown only where the model met its accuracy standard on held-out historical data: today, total volume at every horizon and install and repair volume 5 to 13 weeks ahead. Other slices show only the measured error.

**Question handling rules:**

- One question, one answer; there is no conversation.
- Relative dates such as "last month" use a fixed reference date, 30 August 2026, the end of the dataset.
- With no period given, a default applies and the answer says so: last full calendar month (reporting), last six months (sentiment trends), next month (forecasts).
- Out-of-scope questions are declined with a list of what is supported; questions spanning several capabilities are not answered, so each part is submitted separately.
- Names matching no one, or several people, get a request for the full name and no figures.

## 1.3 Architecture at a Glance

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The platform runs as six services on Google Cloud Run.

1. Gateway. The only internet-facing service; handles the web interface, sign-in, and usage limits, and passes questions to the orchestrator.
2. Orchestrator. Routes each question to a specialist, requests verification, and returns the result.
3. Reporting service. The reporting agent plus its incidents data service.
4. Sentiment service. The sentiment agent plus its feedback data service.
5. Forecast service. The forecast agent plus its volume data service.
6. Verification service. Checks every answer before it is returned, using read-only database access and none of the specialists' tools.

Agents talk over the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol and reach their data services, which hold the database credentials, over the Model Context Protocol (MCP); no component accepts free-form database queries. Supporting components are Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 16, Google Secret Manager, and Google Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.

## 1.4 How a Question Is Answered

1. Sign-in. A personal invite link is exchanged for a session of up to 12 hours.
2. Submission. The gateway checks the session and usage limits and forwards the question; the orchestrator sets a 120-second deadline for all later steps.
3. Routing. One language-model call picks the capability; out-of-scope or multi-capability questions stop here with an explanation.
4. Interpretation and calculation. One language-model call turns the question into a structured request; fixed code then computes every figure from the database, and templates build the answer text.
5. Verification. The verification service independently recomputes every figure and confirms the answer text states only supported numbers. A further language-model call checks that the request matches the question; it is advisory and cannot fail an answer.
6. Result. A passed answer is shown as verified; failed figures withhold the answer and flag it for follow-up; if verification is unavailable, the answer is shown marked "not verified."

Built-in safeguards:

- Deadline. A request reaching 120 seconds stops with a clear warning.
- Circuit breakers. After three failures in a row, a dependency is skipped for 30 seconds while the other capabilities keep answering.
- Cost cap. Each request is capped at an estimated \$0.02 of model usage.
- No customer comments sent to a model. Example comments go straight from the database into the answer template.

## 1.5 Environment and Dependencies

All services run in one Google Cloud project (us-central1) and scale to zero when idle, so the first question after idle starts new instances. The only external runtime dependency is the Google Gemini API.

In testing, six concurrent questions were served by a single instance, so independent scaling across services has not been demonstrated.

Every container has a startup check, and each agent waits for its data service to be ready before it takes requests. The verification agent's startup check confirms only that its process is running, not that its database is reachable. No container has a liveness probe: Cloud Run restarts a container that exits, but not one that hangs.

Neither trained model runs inside a request.

- Sentiment classifier. A fine-tuned BERT classifier labelled every comment in advance; it cannot label new ones.
- Forecast model. A regression model fitted on 156 weeks of history, built into the forecast and verification images.

## 1.6 Security and Access

Users enter only through a personal invite link with an expiry date, revocable within about a minute; only a one-way hash of each invite is stored. Only the gateway is public; every other service accepts calls only from its designated caller.

Each data service has its own least-privilege database role (the forecast service reads three columns of one table). No component that interacts with the language model can read customer contact records, and no credential is stored in code or images.

On 18 October 2026 a credential scan of the full source history and of the nine deployed container images found no credentials; every credential the services use comes from Secret Manager. Secret scanning and push protection are enabled on the source repository. Dependencies are not scanned automatically for known vulnerabilities.

Every service writes structured logs linked by a trace ID. Question text, customer comments, and credentials are not logged. Every web-server access line carries the trace ID and the request's duration. Model-written routing explanations are recorded only as a length and checksum, and internal error messages are recorded as their type, not their text. Two exceptions are known. When a reporting tool refuses a request, the reporting service and its data service log the tool's error text, which can include the dates read from the question; the question wording itself was not seen in the one failure path checked, and other failure paths have not been checked. The model provider's own error sentence for a rejected request is also logged, shortened.

## 1.7 Service Levels and Known Limits

Service hours. The platform is fully available during announced windows. Outside them the database is stopped to control cost, and every data question returns "The data service is unavailable right now. Please try again later." This is the intended state, not a fault.

Response time:

- Most questions are answered in about 4 seconds.
- The first question after an idle period can take about a minute. Measured first answers after an idle period took between 31 and 61 seconds across the reporting, sentiment and forecast paths, all within the 120-second limit.
- No request runs longer than 120 seconds.

Usage limits are 50 questions per day across all users (resets at midnight Pacific) and 30 per invite per hour; see Appendix B.

**Known limits users should understand:**

- What "verified" means. The figures are correct for the request as the platform interpreted it; it does not confirm the question was interpreted correctly, so every answer shows an "Interpreted as" line.
- Ambiguous questions go to the best-fitting capability instead of being returned for clarification.
- The dataset is fixed: it is synthetic, ends on 30 August 2026, and no new feedback comments can be classified.

# 2. Support Model and Severity

## 2.1 Roles and Escalation

The platform has one System Owner, Eric Serrano, responsible for every level of support: answering reports, diagnosing faults, deploying fixes, and recovering the system. A qualified engineer taking over could follow these procedures without the owner's help.

| **Role**                           | **Responsibility**                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Business user**                  | Reads the "Interpreted as" line and verification status on every answer, and reports anything that looks wrong (Section 3).                               |
| **System Owner (Eric Serrano)**    | Runs service windows and access, monitors the system, triages and resolves incidents, deploys changes, and maintains this document.                       |
| **Google Cloud and Google Gemini** | Platform and language-model providers; their outages are handled by waiting, switching keys, or telling users (Sections 5 and 6), not by contacting them. |

**How users report a problem.** Users report problems to the System Owner at [ericserrano2027@u.northwestern.edu](mailto:ericserrano2027@u.northwestern.edu) - Section 3.5 lists what to include.

**What "Sent for follow-up" means.** When an answer is withheld or cannot be completed, the interface shows "Sent for follow-up" with a warning, which flags the request in the logs for review each service window (Section 4) but opens no ticket. A degraded answer sends an email alert to the system owner; the alert was verified end to end on 16 October 2026 with a test entry, and the email arrived within about four minutes. This is the only alert on system behavior, the budget alerts cover spending only.

## 2.2 Severity Levels

Every incident is assigned a severity at first triage and re-assessed as more is learned. Response targets apply during announced service windows.

| **Level** | **Definition**                                                                                      | **Examples**                                                                                                       | **Response target**        | **Resolution target**         |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **SEV1**  | No useful answers during a service window, a wrong figure shown as verified, or a security exposure | Language-model balance runs out mid-window; a credential appears in a log; verification passes an incorrect figure | Acknowledge within 1 hour  | Mitigate within 4 hours       |
| **SEV2**  | One capability is down or degraded while the others answer                                          | Forecast capability returns "temporarily unavailable"; sentiment answers fail because stored labels are incomplete | Acknowledge within 4 hours | Resolve within 1 business day |
| **SEV3**  | Slow or partial service with a workaround                                                           | Unusually slow first answer; misinterpreted question the user rephrased                                            | Next business day          | Next planned change           |
| **SEV4**  | Cosmetic issues or documentation errors                                                             | Unclear answer wording; outdated step in this document                                                             | As time allows             | Next planned change           |

"Mitigate" means stopping the harm, for example by rolling back a release, closing the window, or revoking access, with any permanent fix to follow.

**SEV1 takes priority even when unconfirmed.** A credible report of a wrong verified figure (a confident, incorrect answer given to a decision-maker) or of a security exposure is handled as SEV1 until disproved.

**The following are expected behavior, not incidents:**

- The "data service is unavailable" message outside a service window.
- Declines for out-of-scope questions.
- Requests to use a full name when a name matches no one or several people.
- Reaching the daily or hourly question limit.
- A slow first answer after an idle period that completes within 120 seconds.

## 2.3 Incident Workflow

Incidents follow the same six steps regardless of severity; only the speed and depth of review change.

1. **Detect.** An incident is found through a user report, the test question run when a window opens, or the owner's log review for follow-up flags, failed verification, and error responses.
2. **Triage.** Assign a severity using Section 2.2. Find the request in Google Cloud Logging by time and outcome and follow its trace ID through each service to locate the failed step; use the Section 5 symptom tables to narrow the cause.
3. **Contain.** For SEV1 and SEV2, stop the harm before investigating further: roll back the last release, revoke compromised invites or rotate a key, or close the service window if the platform cannot answer reliably (Sections 4 and 6).
4. **Resolve.** Apply the fix and confirm it with the same test questions used to open a window, one per capability.
5. **Communicate.** For SEV1 and SEV2, tell current invite holders by email what happened, what was affected, and when service resumed or will resume; there is no status page.
6. **Record.** Log every SEV1 and SEV2 in the incident history (Appendix C) with the timeline, cause, fix, and any follow-up work.

SEV1 incidents also get a short written review of what allowed the problem and what prevents it recurring.

# 3. Using the System and Reading Its Responses

This section is for business users. It covers access, good questions, reading responses, and failure messages.

## 3.1 Getting Access

Access is by personal invite link, issued by the System Owner for a set period.

- **Signing in.** Opening the link signs you in for up to 12 hours; reopen it to sign in again.
- **Signing out.** Use the sign-out control; closing the tab does not end the session.
- **Keep the link private.** Anyone with the link can use the platform; if it may have been shared, ask the System Owner to revoke it and issue a new one.
- **Invalid links.** Expired, revoked, and mistyped links get the same refusal by design; ask the System Owner for a new link.

## 3.2 Asking a Good Question

The platform answers one question at a time with no memory of earlier ones, so each question must stand alone. Answers are clearest when the question:

- Asks about one capability: reporting, sentiment, or forecasting (Section 1.2)
- Names the measure: incident count or rate, SLA compliance, first-time fix rate, repeat visits, sentiment, or request volume
- Names the period, such as "July 2026" or "the next 8 weeks" (relative dates use 30 August 2026, so "last month" means July 2026)
- Uses one of the four regions: Northeast, Southeast, Central, or West
- Uses full names for technicians and accounts

## 3.3 Reading a Response

A response is shown in a fixed order. Any part with nothing to show is left out.

**1\. The answer.** The figures and a short explanation, including any assumed period. Grouped results list at most 25 groups, worst first; rates based on fewer than 20 cases are marked as too few to compare reliably.

**2\. The "Interpreted as" line.** It lists the measure, dates (and whether assumed), region ("all regions" or "region not recognised" when it does not apply), account or technician, breakdown, and forecast horizon; if it does not match what you meant, rephrase, since the figures are correct only for the request as shown.

**3\. The verification line.** Every answer is checked by an independent verification service before it is shown. The line reads exactly as follows:

| **Status**  | **What the line says**                                                                                        | **What it means**                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Verified    | "Figures checked for the request as interpreted. Check that the "Interpreted as" line matches your question." | Every figure was recomputed independently and matched. The figures are correct for the request as the platform interpreted it; it does not confirm the question was interpreted correctly. |
| Failed      | "Not verified: the answer failed verification and is not shown."                                              | The figures did not pass the check, so they are withheld.                                                                                                                                  |
| Unavailable | "Not verified: the checking service was unavailable."                                                         | The answer is shown but was not checked. Treat it with caution.                                                                                                                            |
| Not checked | "Not checked: the request ended before verification ran."                                                     | The request stopped early, usually at the time or cost limit.                                                                                                                              |

Declines have no verification line.

On a clarification request, such as a name that matches two technicians, the verification line still appears although no figures were produced; it can be disregarded there.

**4\. Follow-up flag and warning.** When a request could not be completed normally, the response shows "Sent for follow-up" and a warning saying why (the 120-second time limit, the cost limit, an unavailable capability or verification service, or failed verification). The flag records the request for the System Owner's review; report it only if it keeps happening.

Forecast answers also show an 80% range on each weekly figure and the measured historical error, and name periods that cannot be forecast reliably with their error but no numbers.

## 3.4 Messages and What to Do

Some requests end with a fixed message instead of an answer; internal error text is never passed on.

| **Message**                                                                                                     | **Likely reason and what to do**                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "The data service is unavailable right now. Please try again later."                                            | Outside service hours, or a data service is down; report it if it appears during an announced window.       |
| "I couldn't interpret the question. Please rephrase it."                                                        | The question could not be turned into a request; rephrase it (Section 3.2).                                 |
| "The date range in the question can't be answered. Please check the dates and try again."                       | The dates fall outside the dataset (September 2023 to August 2026) or forecast horizon; use another period. |
| "The language model is rate-limited right now. Please try again in about a minute."                             | Too many simultaneous requests; wait a minute and retry.                                                    |
| "The language model is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."                                      | Provider problems; retry in a few minutes and report it if it persists.                                     |
| "The language model's daily quota is used up. It resets at midnight Pacific time."                              | The provider's daily allowance is used up; try again after midnight Pacific.                                |
| "Something went wrong on our side. Please try again."                                                           | An unexpected internal error; retry once, then report it.                                                   |
| "The service could not answer. Please try again."                                                               | An unrecognised failure; retry once, then report it.                                                        |
| "Daily limit reached: this demo answers a fixed number of questions a day. It resets at midnight Pacific time." | The shared limit of 50 questions a day has been reached; try again after midnight Pacific.                  |
| A message that you have asked too many questions this hour                                                      | The limit is 30 per invite per hour; wait for the hour to pass.                                             |

**Declines.** These are answers, not errors: the platform declines, and says why, a question that is out of scope, spans more than one capability (submit each part separately), names an unsupported area or breakdown, or matches no one or several people (the decline lists them so you can ask again with the full name).

## 3.5 When to Report a Problem

Report to the System Owner (Section 2.1) when:

- a verified answer contains a figure you believe is wrong, even if unsure;
- the "Interpreted as" line does not match your question and rephrasing does not help;
- the "data service is unavailable" message appears during an announced service window;
- the same warning or error repeats across several questions.

Include the time, the question as typed, the response, and the "Interpreted as" line.

# 4. Standard Operating Procedures

These procedures cover routine operation of the platform. The System Owner runs all commands (listed in Appendix A) from an administrator workstation with Google Cloud command-line access.

Two conventions apply throughout:

- **One service at a time.** Change one service, confirm it, then move to the next.
- **Record every action** in the operations log (Appendix C): what was done, when, and the result, never a secret, invite link, or token.

## 4.1 Open a Service Window

Open the window the day before it starts, or on the morning of the first day.

1. **Check the language-model balance.** In the Billing console, confirm the prepaid balance is at least \$5 and top it up if lower.
2. **Start the database.** Set it to always-on and wait until it reports running; start-up has taken between 5 and 13 minutes.
3. **Create user invites.** Create one invite per user, set to expire at the end of the window's last day.
   - Use the gateway's primary address; sign-in fails from the older one.
   - Each link is displayed once; store it in a password manager.
   - Send each link to its user with the window's start and end dates.
4. **Renew the owner's invite** if it expires before the window ends, then revoke the old one.
5. **Run the opening test.** Sign in with the owner's link and ask one question per capability (reporting, sentiment, forecast); each answer should show an "Interpreted as" line and a verification line.
   - The first answer may take about a minute while services start.
   - A sentiment question returning "The data service is unavailable" points to incomplete stored labels (Section 5).
6. **Confirm automatic deployment is off.** Check that the build trigger is disabled (Section 4.5).

## 4.2 Close a Service Window

Close the window the day after it ends, no later.

1. **Revoke every user invite** issued for the window.
2. **Stop the database and confirm it reports stopped.** Every data question now returns the "data service is unavailable" message, which is intended.
3. **Record the window** in the operations log:
   - the start and end dates;
   - the balance at opening;
   - when the database was started and stopped;
   - the invites created and revoked, by label and ID only.

## 4.3 Access Management

Invites are managed with an administration tool that reads and writes the invite store in Secret Manager, which holds only a one-way hash of each invite, so lost links are replaced, not recovered.

| **Task**   | **Procedure**                                                                                | **Effect**                                                                    |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Create** | Give a label and a lifetime in days (fractions allowed) and use the primary gateway address. | The link prints once.                                                         |
| **List**   | List all invites.                                                                            | Shows label, ID, expiry and status. Never shows hashes or links.              |
| **Revoke** | Revoke by ID.                                                                                | Takes effect within about 60 seconds and ends any session that invite opened. |

Revoke any invite reported as shared or lost, and every invite issued for a window when it closes.

## 4.4 Monitoring During a Window

**Check once a day during a window, and after any change.**

1. **Reachability.** Request the gateway's public health address and expect a success response. Cloud Run reserves the conventional health path, so the platform uses its own.
2. **Log review.** In Google Cloud Logging, filter the platform's services for degraded or follow-up-flagged answers, error responses, database connection errors ("too many connections"), incomplete stored sentiment labels, and failed language-model calls. Degraded answers return as normal web responses, so Cloud Run's error charts miss them; a degraded answer sends an email alert to the system owner.
3. **Request tracing.** For any problem request, filter on its trace ID to see each service it touched, in order, with its outcome. Every web-server access line carries the trace ID and each request's duration, which shows where time was spent.

**Run the deployment verification script after every change**; it checks the configuration and answers one test question. It covers all six services.

## 4.5 Deploying a Change

**Change control**

- **Automatic deployment is off.** Each deployment of the six services has been a Cloud Build run started by hand while the automatic trigger was disabled, followed by a hand-run verification script. The pipeline's own verification step has not yet run against all six services. The trigger stays disabled outside planned deployment periods.
- **Never enable the trigger before the service definitions match the live system**, or the next deployment moves five services back to the unreliable free model key. The service definitions were brought in line with the live configuration on 14 October 2026, and the deployment verification script confirms each service's model key. Before enabling the trigger, run the script and confirm every check passes.
- **Answer-changing releases need re-evaluation** before release; logging, configuration, or tooling changes may follow normally.

**Procedure**

1. **Start the database first.** A revision whose data service cannot reach the database never takes traffic.
2. **Build.** Build the images, each tagged with its source commit.
3. **Deploy in order.** Deploy one service at a time (verification, sentiment, forecast, reporting, orchestrator, gateway), waiting until each service's newest revision holds 100% of traffic, because deploying all at once could exceed the database's 60-connection limit.
4. **Confirm the configuration:**
   - every service's live revision holds 100% of traffic;
   - each service runs the expected commit tag (read from the service definition);
   - only the gateway is public, and each other service accepts only its designated caller;
   - only the four database-backed services are connected to the database;
   - the sentiment data service runs in stored-labels mode.
5. **Wait, then verify.** After any permission change, wait a few minutes before running the deployment verification script, and expect every check to pass.
6. **Test.** Run the opening test from Section 4.1.

## 4.6 Rollback

A deployment moves traffic to a new revision before verification runs, so a revision that fails verification keeps serving until it is rolled back by hand.

1. List the service's revisions and identify the last good one.
2. Move 100% of traffic to that revision.
3. Confirm the service now reports that revision as serving, then run the opening test.

Re-running a deployment from the same commit does not replace a failed revision; roll back or deploy a corrected commit. A service with no earlier revision cannot be rolled back; remove its caller permission and delete it only after confirming nothing depends on it.

## 4.7 Secrets and Key Rotation

All credentials live in Secret Manager, readable only by the service accounts that need them (Appendix B lists them).

**Handling rules**

- Generate new values fresh and pipe them straight into Secret Manager.
- Never type values on a command line, print them, or copy them from a development machine.
- On the Windows workstation, save a secret without a trailing line break.

**Rotating a secret.** Add a new version, then roll each service that uses it so new instances read the new value. A database password also needs changing in the database, as administrator through the secure proxy; rotating the session signing key signs out every user; invite-store changes take effect within about 60 seconds without a restart.

Rotation has not yet been exercised on the live system, so do the first one in a deployment period, not a service window.

## 4.8 Cost Monitoring

Review costs at each window opening and close.

| **Cost**                                                   | **Approximate amount** |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Database while running                                     | \$0.30 per day         |
| Database storage while stopped                             | \$0.06 per day         |
| Language-model use at the full daily limit of 50 questions | \$0.35 per day         |
| Cloud Run when idle                                        | Nothing                |

**Spending ceilings.** Spending is bounded by budget alerts at \$10 on the language-model project and at \$50 and \$80 on the billing account; a prepaid model-API balance with automatic top-up turned off, which is the hard stop on model spending; a per-question cost cap; and limits of 30 questions per invite per hour and 50 per day. The question limits are held in the gateway's memory, and the gateway runs as a single instance: the daily limit is shared by all users and resets at midnight Pacific, and both limits also reset if the gateway restarts.

## 4.9 Security Patching

Every software dependency is pinned to an exact version, and the build fails if the pins are inconsistent. Watch vendor security advisories for the web framework and the language-model and protocol libraries, and assess whether the vulnerable code path is reachable in this deployment. Pin only to a version a published advisory names as fixed, then rebuild, run the dependency audit by hand, and confirm it reports no high-severity vulnerabilities. Redeploy only the affected service, where possible, the patch release changes no answers. Check the language-model provider's deprecation notices before each service window as well. The platform is pinned to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, which had no announced shutdown date on 22 October 2026 and a retirement or redirect of that model would change the platform's behavior without any code change.

**Worked example (October 2026).** Three critical and high-severity web-framework advisories were unreachable because the interface is pre-built static files, yet the framework was upgraded to the fixed version as a precaution, deployed on 14 October 2026.

## 4.10 Data Maintenance

The dataset is fixed. Its only routine maintenance is the stored sentiment labels.

- **Re-label after every data reload.** A reload clears the stored labels, so re-run the labelling job and confirm its fingerprint equals the recorded 7,521 rows exactly, or keep sentiment out of service until the mismatch is explained.
- **Re-label after a classifier change.** Labels are stored per version, so a new classifier version needs a full re-labelling run while earlier answers stay traceable to the model that produced them.
- **Forecast model files** are built into the forecast and verification images, and both verify the files' checksums at start-up. A changed or missing file stops the service.

# 5. Troubleshooting

## 5.1 Sign-In and Access

| **Symptom**                       | **Severity**                                              | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                                                            | **Resolution**                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The page loads but sign-in fails. | SEV3, or SEV1 if no user can sign in during a window      | Invite expired, revoked, or copied incompletely, or the link uses Cloud Run's older address; list invites to confirm this one is active and uses the primary address. | Issue a new invite on the primary address (Section 4.3).                                             |
| A revoked invite still works.     | SEV1 after 60 seconds; normal within the first 60 seconds | Revocations take up to 60 seconds; beyond that, access control has failed; wait 70 seconds, then retry.                                                               | If it still works, remove the gateway's public access at once, revoke every invite, and investigate. |

## 5.2 "The data service is unavailable right now"

| **Symptom**                                                     | **Severity**                               | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                    | **Resolution**                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Every question gets this message.                               | SEV1 during a window; expected outside one | Database stopped (normal outside a window, an error during one); confirm its state and activation policy.                     | Start it and wait for running (5 to 13 minutes); run the opening test.    |
| Only sentiment questions get this message.                      | SEV2                                       | Some comments in the period have no stored label; look for "stored predictions incomplete" in the sentiment service's logs.   | Re-run the offline labelling job; confirm its fingerprint (Section 4.10). |
| One capability gets this message while the database is running. | SEV2                                       | Its data service cannot reach the database, or its query is failing; read its logs for readiness failures or database errors. | Fix the cause; if it began after a release, roll back (Section 4.6).      |

These requests are not flagged: a database failure during a window returns this error message, not a flagged degraded answer (a known limitation), so search for error responses instead of follow-up flags.

## 5.3 Degraded Answers ("Sent for follow-up")

The warning names the reason. Find the request's trace ID before acting.

A degraded result was observed live on 13 October 2026, on the previous build, when a model-provider outage made the routing step time out at 30 seconds. None has occurred on the current build.

| **Symptom**                                                | **Severity**                              | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | **Resolution**                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Time limit reached."                                      | SEV3, or SEV2 if it repeats               | Slow model calls, several cold services starting at once, or a dependency that stopped responding; follow the trace ID to the slow step; each service's access line shows its duration.                                                     | Retry a single slow request; fix an unresponsive dependency.            |
| "\[Capability\] is temporarily unavailable."               | SEV2                                      | A dependency failed three times in a row; its circuit breaker opened for 30 seconds; read the named service's logs for start-up failures, crashes, or timeouts.                                                                             | Fix the service; the breaker closes after one successful trial call.    |
| "Verification unavailable" (answer shown as not verified). | SEV2                                      | Verification service down, timed out, or cannot reach the database; read its logs (it refuses to start if its forecast model files fail their checksum).                                                                                    | Restore it; until then treat answers as unchecked.                      |
| "Failed verification" (answer withheld).                   | SEV1 until disproved                      | A specialist's figure did not match the independent recomputation, so the specialist or the verification service is wrong (never retried); read the failed checks in the logs and reproduce the question and compare with a database query. | Roll back if it followed a release, and never weaken or skip the check. |
| "Cost limit reached."                                      | SEV2                                      | One request used over about \$0.02 of model calls, pointing to a loop or unexpected retries; follow the trace ID and count the calls.                                                                                                       | Fix the cause before reopening the capability.                          |
| Warning names "routing".                                   | SEV2, or SEV1 if it lasts during a window | The language model could not classify the question.                                                                                                                                                                                         | See Section 5.4.                                                        |

## 5.4 Language-Model Provider Problems

| **Symptom**                                                             | **Severity**                        | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **Resolution**                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rate-limited, unavailable, or slow model responses.                     | SEV2 or SEV3, depending on duration | Provider overloaded or limiting requests; failed calls are retried a limited number of times; check the logs for failed model-call lines. Each failed attempt is logged with its error type, status and wait time; the question text and key are never logged. (deployed; not yet observed, because no failed attempt has occurred) | Wait and retry; as a last resort, switch to the free key (it failed repeatedly on 13 October 2026 while the paid service answered). |
| Every question fails during a window, and the balance may be exhausted. | SEV1                                | Prepaid balance has run out, so no question can be answered; read the balance in the Billing console (behavior at exhaustion is untested).                                                                                                                                                                                          | Top up with no redeployment; keep the opening rule of at least \$5 before every window.                                             |

## 5.5 Slow Responses

A slow first answer is expected (see Section 1.7); if one service alone takes more than 40 seconds to start, or first answers approach 120 seconds, record it.

## 5.6 Deployment Problems

| **Symptom**                                                             | **Severity**                                           | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                                                           | **Resolution**                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A new revision never becomes ready.                                     | SEV3; users keep being served by the previous revision | Database stopped during deployment, or a configuration error (malformed setting, model file failing its checksum) stopped the service; read the new revision's logs. | Fix the cause, then deploy a change that creates a new revision; re-running the same commit leaves the failed one. |
| A revision is serving but failed verification.                          | SEV2, or SEV1 if answers are affected                  | A deployment moves traffic before verification runs; see which checks failed.                                                                                        | Roll back (Section 4.6), then investigate.                                                                         |
| A service refuses calls from its designated caller just after a change. | SEV3                                                   | A new access permission has not applied yet (this has taken more than a minute); retry after a few minutes.                                                          | Usually none; if it persists, compare the permission with the expected configuration.                              |

## 5.7 Database

| **Symptom**                                 | **Severity** | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Resolution**                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Too many connections" in a service's logs. | SEV2         | The database allows 60 connections. In steady state the services use at most 32 connections; during a one-at-a-time deployment, at most 40. Several services were deployed at once, or administrator sessions were left open. | Close administrator sessions and let old revisions drain; deploy one service at a time. |
| The database takes a long time to start.    | SEV3         | Normal variation (starts of up to 13 minutes seen); if not running after 20 minutes, check its operation status in the Cloud SQL console.                                                                                     | Open the window only after the database is running and the opening test passes.         |

## 5.8 Answer-Quality Concerns

| **Symptom**                                                                                  | **Severity**                                                  | **Likely cause and check**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | **Resolution**                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A verified answer addresses the wrong question.                                              | SEV3 if the user caught it; SEV1 if a decision was made on it | Misinterpreted question: the figures are correct for the request as the platform interpreted it; it does not confirm the question was interpreted correctly; compare the "Interpreted as" line with the question; the logs record the structured request. | The user rephrases; record recurring patterns; changing interpretation needs re-evaluation before release. |
| An ambiguous question was answered by one capability.                                        | SEV4                                                          | Known limitation: ambiguous questions go to the best-fitting capability.                                                                                                                                                                                  | The user rephrases with a specific measure (Section 3.2).                                                  |
| A future-tense question about an unsupported subject is declined with a forecasting message. | SEV4                                                          | Future-tense questions go to the forecast capability, which declines subjects it cannot forecast; the message lists only forecasting coverage.                                                                                                            | None needed; the user can rephrase.                                                                        |
| Example comments don't match the trend.                                                      | SEV4                                                          | With no label requested, examples are chosen by classifier confidence, which favours the most common label, usually positive.                                                                                                                             | Ask for examples by label, such as "show negative comments".                                               |

# 6. Disaster Recovery

This section covers recovery from failures that the troubleshooting steps in Section 5 cannot fix, from database loss to loss of the administrator workstation.

## 6.1 Recovery Posture and Objectives

**Data protection rests on reproducibility, not backups**: the database has no automated backups or point-in-time recovery, which is defensible only because the platform holds no data that cannot be rebuilt exactly:

- **The dataset is synthetic and deterministic**, checked against a recorded reference.
- **Sentiment labels are reproduced by re-running the labelling job and must match a recorded fingerprint.**
- **Users create no data; the only records are** the invite store and the operations log.
- Code and service definitions are in version control, images in Artifact Registry, secrets in Secret Manager.

A production system holding real customer data could not rely on this; it would need backups and tested restores (Section 6.3).

The database runs as a single-zone instance in one region (us-central1). Recovery means rebuilding it from the deterministic generator and the frozen comment corpus, then regenerating and loading the offline-scored sentiment predictions.

| **Scenario**                                 | **Recovery time objective**                      | **Recovery point objective**        |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| Bad release                                  | 15 minutes                                       | No data loss                        |
| Credential compromise                        | 1 hour to contain; rotation as soon as practical | No data loss                        |
| Database loss or corruption                  | 2 hours                                          | No data loss (data rebuilt exactly) |
| Language-model provider outage               | Dependent on the provider                        | Not applicable                      |
| Regional outage or loss of the cloud project | 1 business day                                   | No data loss; invites reissued      |

These objectives are estimates from measured step times (database creation in under 10 minutes, schema build in under 30 seconds); full rebuilds have not been rehearsed.

## 6.2 Recovery Scenarios

Each scenario ends with the clean restart in Section 7, which brings the platform back in a verified order. Commands are in Appendix A.

### 6.2.1 Database Loss or Corruption

Use this procedure when the database instance is deleted or unrecoverable, or its data is wrong.

1. Recreate the instance (PostgreSQL 16, Enterprise edition, smallest shared-core tier, connection limit raised to 60), or keep it if only the data is affected.
2. Set the administrator password from Secret Manager and create the application database.
3. Connect through the secure database proxy from the administrator workstation; never open an authorized network.
4. Build the schema: apply the migrations as the administrator (every table, seven roles, permissions).
5. Load the dataset as the generator role, in one transaction.
6. Validate the data: run the validation suite (all 67 checks pass) and the permissions test suite.
7. Re-run the offline labelling job as the sentiment role; the fingerprint must show 7,521 rows and the recorded checksum.
8. Restart the platform (Section 7); if the instance was renamed, first update the connection in the four database-backed services.

### 6.2.2 Bad Release

A release that produces wrong answers, fails verification, or fails to start is recovered by rollback (Section 4.6): move 100% of traffic back to the last good revision of each affected service, one at a time, then run the opening test. If the release changed answers, check the logged verification failures and tell affected users (Section 2.3).

### 6.2.3 Credential Compromise

Treat any suspected exposure as SEV1. Contain first, then rotate (Section 4.7).

| **Credential**             | **Containment**                                                                    | **Rotation**                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Invite link**            | Revoke the invite. Takes effect within about 60 seconds and ends its sessions.     | Issue a new invite to the legitimate holder.                                                      |
| **Language-model key**     | Disable the key with the provider. Questions fail until a replacement is in place. | Create a new key, add it as a new secret version, and roll the five services that call the model. |
| **Database role password** | Change the role's password in the database at once.                                | Add it as a new secret version and roll the data service that uses it.                            |
| **Gateway session key**    | Rotate it immediately; every session is signed out.                                | Users sign in again with their existing invites.                                                  |
| **Administrator password** | Change it in the database at once.                                                 | Store the new value in Secret Manager; no service reads it.                                       |

After containment, review the logs for activity during the exposure and find how the credential leaked before reopening service.

### 6.2.4 Language-Model Provider Outage

The platform depends on one language-model provider; without it, no question can be answered.

- **Short outage:** wait; the circuit breaker prevents a pile-up of failing calls and users see a clear unavailability warning.
- **Failure of the paid service alone:** switch to the free key with one configuration change (Section 5.4), a last resort because the free service was unreliable in October 2026.
- **Extended outage:** close the window (Section 4.2) and tell users when it is expected to reopen.

A second provider could be added behind the single language-model interface, but that is a code change requiring re-evaluation, not an outage recovery action.

### 6.2.5 Regional Outage or Loss of the Cloud Project

The platform runs in one region (us-central1) with no standby; in a regional outage, wait for Google to restore service, and if the outage is prolonged or the project is lost (deleted, locked, or compromised), rebuild in a new project or region:

1. Prepare the project: create the project, link billing, set the \$50 and \$80 budget alerts, enable the required services, and create the image repository and service accounts.
2. Create every secret with newly generated values; old values are treated as lost.
3. Rebuild the database (Section 6.2.1, steps 1 to 7).
4. Deploy the services one at a time (Section 4.5), then apply the caller permissions so only the gateway is public.
5. Run the deployment verification script and the opening test.
6. Issue new invites on the new gateway address and notify users.

The language-model key and its prepaid balance live in a separate project; if it survives, reuse the key, otherwise create and fund a new one before reopening.

### 6.2.6 Loss of the Administrator Workstation

Source code, service definitions, and the frozen corpus are in version control, so a replacement workstation needs only the Google Cloud command-line tools, the database proxy, and the project's pinned Python environment.

**Trained models.** The sentiment classifier, with its training runs and checkpoints, is held on the administrator workstation, and a second copy is kept in the System Owner's private cloud storage; on 18 October 2026 each of the copy's five files was confirmed byte-identical to the recorded checksums.

To restore it:

1. Copy the classifier folder onto the replacement workstation.
2. Re-run the offline labelling job; it refuses to run if any model file differs from the recorded checksums.
3. Confirm that the resulting fingerprint matches the reference.

The forecast model files are under version control and need no separate copy.

## 6.3 What a Production Deployment Would Add

The controls below would be required for a platform holding real business data; they are recorded here as known gaps, not omissions.

| **Control**            | **Production expectation**                                                      | **Status here and why**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Database backups       | Daily automated backups with point-in-time recovery, and periodic test restores | Off; data is synthetic and rebuilt exactly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Recovery rehearsal     | Scheduled disaster-recovery drills                                              | Not yet run; objectives above are estimates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Model artifact storage | Versioned off-machine storage for every trained model                           | Forecast model: version control. Sentiment classifier: workstation plus private cloud copy, checked against recorded checksums on use; second copy confirmed identical on 18 October 2026; not versioned storage.                                                       |
| Alerting               | Automatic alerts on degraded answers and errors                                 | A degraded answer sends an email alert to the system owner; the alert was verified end to end on 16 October 2026 with a test entry, and the email arrived within about four minutes. This is the only alert on system behaviour; the budget alerts cover spending only. |
| Second operator        | At least two people able to run recovery                                        | One owner; this document is the handover.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

# 7. Clean Restart Procedure

A clean restart brings the existing deployment back to a known-good state in a fixed order, confirming each layer before starting the next. Use it:

- after database recovery (Section 6.2.1);
- after a platform-wide failure has been fixed;
- when services are behaving inconsistently and the cause is unclear;
- before reopening a window that was closed because of an incident.

Rebuilding the platform from nothing is a different procedure, covered in Section 6.2.5.

**Do not start a phase until the previous phase's gate has passed; if a gate fails, stop and see the table at the end. Commands are in Appendix A.**

## Phase 1: Prepare

1. **Notify users.** If a window is open, tell them the platform is restarting and roughly when it will return.
2. **Confirm the balance.** The language-model balance must be at least \$5 (Section 4.1).
3. **Confirm automatic deployment is disabled, so no merged change deploys mid-restart.**
4. **Confirm no deployment is in progress** and no administrator database sessions are open.
5. **Confirm every secret listed in Appendix B exists in Secret Manager.**

**Gate:** balance confirmed, trigger disabled, no deployment running, all secrets present.

## Phase 2: Database

1. **Start the database** if it is stopped. Wait until it reports running and always-on (allow up to 20 minutes).
2. **Confirm the sentiment labels.** Through the secure database proxy as the evaluation role, run the label fingerprint check; it must report 7,521 rows and the recorded checksum exactly.
3. **If the database was rebuilt, also confirm the validation and permissions test suites passed (Section 6.2.1).**

**Gate: the database is running and the fingerprint matches. If it does not, the restart may continue, but sentiment stays out of service until resolved (Section 4.10).**

## Phase 3: Services

Choose one of two ways to give the services fresh instances.

**Idle restart (preferred when time allows).** Send no traffic for about 15 minutes; idle instances shut down on their own and the next request starts fresh ones, with no configuration change.

**Forced restart (when service is needed sooner).** Create a new revision of each service from its current image by updating a restart marker in its configuration, and record the marker in the operations log; the next normal deployment replaces it. This method has not yet been rehearsed on the deployed system.

Work through the services one at a time, in this order:

1. Verification
2. Sentiment
3. Forecast
4. Reporting
5. Orchestrator
6. Gateway

Within each specialist, the data service must pass its readiness check, including reaching the database, before its agent starts.

**Gate for each service:** its newest revision is ready and holds 100% of traffic. Only then move to the next.

## Phase 4: Verify the Configuration

1. **Run the deployment verification script** and confirm every check passes. The script checks all six services.
2. **Confirm the configuration from Section 4.5, step 4.**
3. **Confirm the gateway answers** its public health address.

**Gate:** every check passes.

## Phase 5: Functional Test

1. **Sign in** with the owner's invite. Renew it first if it is close to expiry.
2. **Ask one question per capability:**
   - **Reporting:** "What was SLA compliance in the Northeast last month?"
   - **Forecast:** "How many service requests should we expect over the next 4 weeks?"
   - **Sentiment:** "Is customer sentiment trending down in the West?"
3. **Check each response** for an "Interpreted as" line that matches the question, a verification line reading "Figures checked for the request as interpreted", and no follow-up flag.
4. **Check the logs** for the three requests by trace ID. Confirm no errors, degraded results, or failed model calls.

**Gate:** all three questions answered and verified, with clean logs.

## Phase 6: Reopen

1. **Confirm users can sign in.** If invites were revoked or the session key was rotated, issue new invites (Section 4.3).
2. **Tell users** the platform is available, and state the window's remaining dates.
3. **Record the restart** in the operations log (Appendix C): the reason, any gate that failed and how it was resolved, and any restart marker applied.

**When a Gate Fails**

| **Gate**                                       | **Stop and see**                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Phase 1: balance below \$5                     | Top up before continuing (Section 5.4)                                  |
| Phase 1: a secret missing                      | Credential handling (Section 6.2.3)                                     |
| Phase 2: database not running after 20 minutes | Database start problems (Section 5.7)                                   |
| Phase 2: fingerprint mismatch                  | Data maintenance (Section 4.10); continue with sentiment out of service |
| Phase 3: a revision does not become ready      | Deployment problems (Section 5.6); roll that service back (Section 4.6) |
| Phase 3: "too many connections"                | Database connections (Section 5.7)                                      |
| Phase 4: a verification check fails            | Roll back the affected service (Section 4.6)                            |
| Phase 5: an answer is degraded or unverified   | Degraded answers (Section 5.3)                                          |
| Phase 5: "data service is unavailable"         | Data service unavailable (Section 5.2)                                  |

# Appendices

## Appendix A: Command Reference

All commands are written for Windows PowerShell 5.1 on the administrator workstation, signed in to the Google Cloud command-line tools. Values in angle brackets are placeholders. Quote every comma-separated list; PowerShell 5.1 otherwise splits it into separate values.

**Session variables (set once per terminal)**

\$P = '&lt;project-id&gt;'

\$R = 'us-central1'

\$G = '&lt;gateway primary address&gt;'

### A.1 Database

| **Task**                | **Command**                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Start                   | gcloud sql instances patch ops-db --activation-policy ALWAYS --project \$P                            |
| Stop                    | gcloud sql instances patch ops-db --activation-policy NEVER --project \$P                             |
| Check state             | gcloud sql instances describe ops-db --project \$P --format "value(state,settings.activationPolicy)"  |
| Secure admin connection | cloud-sql-proxy &lt;project&gt;:&lt;region&gt;:ops-db --port 5433 (leave running in its own terminal) |

**Expected state:** RUNNABLE ALWAYS when started, STOPPED NEVER when stopped.

### A.2 Services and Traffic

| **Task**                             | **Command**                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| Serving revision                     | gcloud run services describe &lt;service&gt; --region \$R --project \$P --format "value(status.traffic\[0\].revisionName)"                                         |
| Roll back                            | gcloud run services update-traffic &lt;service&gt; --to-revisions &lt;previous-revision&gt;=100 --region \$R --project \$P                                         |
| Check callers                        | gcloud run services get-iam-policy &lt;service&gt; --region \$R --project \$P                                                                                      |
| Forced restart _(not yet rehearsed)_ | gcloud run services update &lt;service&gt; --container &lt;agent-container&gt; --update-env-vars "RESTART_MARKER=&lt;yyyymmdd-hhmm&gt;" --region \$R --project \$P |
| Check auto-deploy is off             | gcloud builds triggers describe deploy-reporting-slice --region \$R --project \$P --format "value(disabled)" (expect True)                                         |

| **Setting**                        | **Value**                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Request deadline                   | 120 seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Circuit breaker                    | Opens after 3 consecutive failures; 30-second cool-down; one trial call                                                                                                                                     |
| Verification retries               | At most 2, for interpretation failures only; never for figure failures                                                                                                                                      |
| Cost cap per request               | \$0.02 (estimated)                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Daily question limit (all users)   | 50, reset at midnight Pacific                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Hourly question limit (per invite) | 30 per invite per hour                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Session length                     | 12 hours or invite expiry, if sooner                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Revocation delay                   | Up to 60 seconds                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Database                           | PostgreSQL 16, smallest shared-core tier, 10 GB, 60 connections, public address with no authorized networks; reached only through Cloud Run's built-in connection or the secure database proxy, backups off |
| Database connections per instance  | At most 4; database-backed services run at most 2 instances each                                                                                                                                            |

**Secrets (names only)**

| **Secret**                    | **Purpose**                                                               |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| gemini-api-key-paid           | Paid language-model key (in use)                                          |
| gemini-api-key                | Free language-model key (fallback)                                        |
| db-role-&lt;role&gt;-password | One per database role; each runtime role readable only by its own service |
| db-admin-password             | Database administrator; readable by no service                            |
| gateway-session-key           | Signs user sessions                                                       |
| gateway-invites               | Invite store (hashes only)                                                |

| 8 Oct 2026  | SEV3         | A new revision never became ready                                               | A change was merged while the database was stopped                                                                        | Expected protective behavior.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 8 Oct 2026  | SEV3         | Verification reported two false failures                                        | One check used a reserved path; another ran before a new permission applied                                               | Check corrected; operators now wait a few minutes after permission changes.                                                                                                                                                          |
